memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Do not set up any wooden Asherah pole beside the altar you build to the Lord your God, and do not erect a sacred stone, for these the Lord your God hates. - Deut 16:21-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends with a firm warning against mixing false worship into true worship. The people were not to plant an Asherah pole or set up a sacred stone beside God's altar. These were symbols of the pagan religions around them, and God says plainly that He hates them.

That is strong language, but it flows from God's love. He knew that even a little idolatry mixed into their worship would slowly poison the whole nation and pull their hearts away from Him. God does not share His people's affection with false gods. He wants worship that is wholehearted and pure, not a blend of Him and everything else.

We may not set up wooden poles, but the temptation to mix worship remains. We can try to hold on to God while also giving our hearts to money, status, comfort, or approval. The New Testament is just as direct, warning us to flee from idolatry and to keep ourselves from idols (1 John 5:21). This is not because God is insecure, but because He knows we were made to find our all in Him. Anything we add alongside Him as a rival will only diminish us. Christ gave Himself fully for us; He is worthy of undivided hearts. Is there anything you have quietly set up beside God that He is calling you to tear down?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What competes with God for your heart's devotion?
2. Why do you think God speaks so strongly against mixed worship?
3. What "pole" might He be asking you to remove?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You alone are worthy of my whole heart. Tear down every rival within me and make my worship pure. Amen.
